listing.name: Halo: Combat Evolved / OpenCE (OpenCommunityEdition)
listing.summary: Play Halo: Combat Evolved through OpenCE with your own Xbox disc image.

steps.title: Choose your original Xbox disc image on first Play
steps.instruction: On first Play, select your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox .iso or .xiso; every edition works. OpenCE extracts its maps into the maps folder beside the player. Keep the disc image outside the game folder, because the game offers any image it finds there. Halo PC or Custom Edition maps do not replace these Xbox maps.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Extract halo-windows-release.zip, or halo-linux-release.zip on Linux, into its own folder and start halo.exe (halo on Linux) from it with no arguments. The release package is for playing; debug builds stop at failed assertions, and symbol archives are not players. OpenCE asks before installing its own updates and can replace its program files when you accept.

warnings: OpenCE is a port of a Halo: Combat Evolved decompilation; the project’s AGPL licence does not cover the original game code. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Optional Halo Custom Edition maps and their matching resources belong in custom_maps. OpenSauce maps are incompatible.
Clicking a Halo or Discord invite starts OpenCE directly, outside Portcove. Close any game started that way before updating or rolling back in Portcove.

references.title: Keep all actual data locations
references.instruction: Beside the program OpenCE keeps config.toml, the extracted maps, custom_maps, mods, load_order.toml, screenshots, logs and crash reports. Profiles, saves and the shader cache are in AppData/Roaming/halo on Windows unless paths.saves or HALO_SAVE_ROOT changes it. In a copy you manage yourself, back these up before an update.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, select your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox .iso or .xiso; OpenCE extracts about 2 GB of maps into the maps folder of the managed game folder. Keep the disc image outside the game folder. Portcove starts OpenCE with its automatic updates and dedicated-server updates turned off, so only Portcove replaces the managed program. Portcove keeps config.toml, maps, custom_maps, mcc_maps, mods, load_order.toml, screenshots, logs, captures, crash reports, init.txt, menus, bans.txt, player.key and the pass files across updates, backups and rollback. Profiles, saves and the shader cache stay in %APPDATA%\halo, which Portcove does not back up or roll back. After a crash, OpenCE's crash reporter may stay open asking whether to send a report, and Portcove keeps tracking it. Internet play registers Halo and Discord invite links that start OpenCE directly, outside Portcove and without the update setting. Close a game started from an invite before updating or rolling back; if you accept an update in a game started that way, Portcove holds the changed copy until you repair it. Turning off CHECK FOR UPDATES in OpenCE's settings also protects those launches. The program is 32-bit Windows.
